definition: Two-point discrimination is a somatosensory measure of whether a person can tell that two nearby touches on the skin are separate rather than a single touch. In this packet, it is used as a sensory test of the upper extremity or dominant hand.

reasons: The packet supports that two-point discrimination was used as a sensory test of the dominant hand or upper extremity, but it does not define the term as the ability to distinguish two nearby skin touches from one touch.
